intended_object: This is the recursively defined sequence of coefficients of the compositional inverse Q of a power series P = uX + O(X²) with u invertible, i.e. the Q with P(Q(X)) = X. The docstring and its only use, `substInv P := .mk (substInvFun P)`, show this.
explanation:
`substInvFun` is a helper used to build `PowerSeries.substInv`, the compositional inverse. It sets the coefficient of X⁰ to 0 and the coefficient of X¹ to u⁻¹. For each later coefficient, it truncates Q at the coefficients already found, substitutes that truncation into P, and corrects the next coefficient so that the coefficient of P(Q) at that degree becomes 0.

The mathematical object here is the compositional inverse `substInv`, not this coefficient function. In the same file, `substInv` is shown to satisfy P(Q) = X (`subst_substInv_right`) and Q(P) = X (`subst_substInv_left`), and to be the unique such inverse.

The recursion itself is sound. Base case: with n = 0, the sum over `Fin 1` is C(0)·1 = 0, so P(0) has coefficient 0 at X¹. The general step follows the standard coefficient-matching argument. The definition needs only a commutative ring R in which u = coeff 1 P is invertible, which is the natural setting.

Since this is an auxiliary construction, not a standard notion in the literature, it is classified as a technical device.
